question: Does rotation compensation make the same short-history constant-velocity pedestrian predictor more useful?
scope: Small offline mechanism feasibility analysis, not a learned model or RGB-only deployment result.
selection: Reuse ALL four previously selected SAM2 long tracks and exact ranges from outputs/sam2_forecast_20260928/candidates.json; do not select on new errors.
point: Visible SAM mask bounding-box center. Not a 3D pedestrian root or manually verified ground truth.
predictor: Ordinary least-squares slope over all six historic native 10Hz center coordinates, anchored at the last observed point; identical formula in raw and normalized coordinates. No training or tuning.
compensation: K R_current_world R_world_past K^-1 rotation warp into the prediction-cutoff camera orientation. Translation/depth/parallax remain.
camera_reference: Existing offline closed-loop MPS orientation, factory RGB extrinsic, linear image intrinsics, timestamp SLERP. All MPS-assisted methods are privileged offline diagnostics, including their historical inputs.
alignment: Bracketing gaps <= 5ms, MPS quality >=0.5, same graph for entire history+target interval, valid unit rotations. Invalid windows excluded from ALL arms with reason logged.

arms.stationary: Sanity baseline: hold last image center.
arms.raw_cv: OLS center velocity in original image coordinates.
arms.comp_cv_predcam: Same OLS in rotation-normalized coordinates; predict future relative camera rotation by OLS slope of historical SO(3) rotation vectors relative to cutoff. No future poses passed to predictor.
arms.comp_cv_refcam: IDENTICAL compensated pedestrian forecast, reprojected with actual future MPS reference rotations. FUTURE-INFORMATION DIAGNOSTIC ONLY, not a causal model or guaranteed mathematical upper bound.

geometry_failure: All denominators/depth signs logged. Nonprojectable forecasts receive fixed 10x image-diagonal error per failed step in headline summary; common fully projectable subset also reported if needed. Finite out-of-frame forecasts are never clipped for metrics.
metrics: Original 2560x1920 image pixel center Euclidean ADE/FDE at 0.5, 1.0, 1.5s; identical windows and target labels across arms; mean, median and per-track paired comparisons.
sensitivity: Report fixed stride 20 frames (nonoverlapping target intervals), no-edge (all history/target boxes >5px from image boundary), equal-track/equal-recording averages, camera rotation strata <5deg, 5-15deg, >=15deg over horizon. No significance claim from overlapping windows.
background_check: Every tenth frame within each selected range, measure next-frame sparse KLT correspondence residual before/after Aria rotation and inverse-rotation negative control. Mask existing SAM person boxes, use FB/NCC filtering independent of Aria; candidates are not manually verified static background.
fixed_examples: One window per track: cutoff start+50 frames, rounded to closest evaluation cutoff. Not chosen by errors.
verification: Identity warp equals raw predictor; rotation sign and inverse tests; known synthetic constant reference-plane velocity plus rotating camera; future suffix perturbation changes only reference-camera diagnostic; independent metrics and source hashes.
limitations: selected surviving SAM tracks, assistant sampled identity review only
rotation-only normalization does not recover pure pedestrian/world motion
MPS closed-loop output is offline estimated reference, not ground truth or causal RGB estimation
future reference camera removes one uncertainty using privileged information
no architecture fusion or training job
